clue.text: Politician very lively at social event?

definitions.text: Politician very lively at social event?

parts.note: surface reading: a party member, someone central to a political organisation
setter's reading: the most energetic, entertaining guest at a gathering

explanation.walkthrough: 'Politician' points to a political party, but the party here is a social one; the phrase describes the guest who keeps everyone entertained.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names the person whose energy and humour make a gathering lively, and 'party' doubles as a political grouping.

clue.text: System of weights used for precious metals in ancient city

definitions.text: System of weights used for precious metals
definitions.meaning: first meaning: the weight system for gold and silver
second meaning: the city besieged by the Greeks in Homer's Iliad

explanation.surface: Gold and silver are being weighed in some old city.
explanation.definitionFit: Troy weight is the standard measure for precious metals, and Troy is the legendary city of the Trojan War.

clue.text: British painter and philanthropist beheaded

indicators.note: losing the head means the word's first letter is cut away

parts.note: J. Paul Getty, oil billionaire whose wealth funds the Getty museum and trust

explanation.surface: A British artist who was also a philanthropist met a grisly end.
explanation.definitionFit: William Etty was a nineteenth-century English painter known for his nudes and history pictures.

clue.text: Plant in pond, and clay pipe, oddly

indicators.note: doing something oddly means in a strange way, so the letters come out in an unusual order

explanation.surface: Someone has found a plant growing in a pond beside an old clay pipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant in pond' reads like a water plant, but 'in' and 'and' are just joins: the fodder is 'pond' plus 'clay pipe'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iceland poppy is an Arctic flowering species grown widely in gardens for its papery blooms.

clue.text: Joy, family member appearing topless

indicators.note: without a top means the word's first letter has gone

explanation.surface: A happy scene: a relative turns up without a top on.
explanation.definitionFit: Elation is a feeling of great happiness, a straightforward synonym for joy.

clue.text: Two things used in tennis game

parts.note: a tennis court is divided by a net
the other item: what the players hit

explanation.surface: Listing equipment needed to play tennis.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'two things' are the two halves of the answer, both genuine tennis equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: Netball is a team sport, mainly played in Britain and the Commonwealth, where players shoot a ball through a high hoop.

clue.text: See 1
For a starter, publisher is entertaining ten on new A list circuit

indicators.note: a host entertaining guests has them inside, so one piece sits within the other
in a down clue, one piece sitting on another goes above it
making something new means remaking it, so the letters that follow are rearranged

parts.note: a circuit is a ring, the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: A publisher hosts a starry dinner with a celebrity guest list going round the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For a starter' is the definition, not a first-letter signal. 'Circuit' adds its ring-shaped letter to the shuffle, and the publisher is the one behind the Oxford dictionaries.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxtail soup is a classic first course, so it is something served for a starter.

clue.text: Officer in place with leaseholder

parts.note: lieu means place, as in 'in lieu of'
a tenant holds a property on a lease

explanation.surface: An officer is billeted with someone renting the property.
explanation.definitionFit: A lieutenant is a commissioned officer rank in the army or navy.

clue.text: See 1
Filthy place close to stable, an eyesore

parts.note: a pigsty, or any squalid place

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is kept

explanation.surface: A dirty pigsty next to the stables spoils the view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eyesore' normally means an ugly sight; here it is read literally as a sore on the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an inflamed swelling on the eyelid, so literally a sore on the eye.

clue.text: Hebridean island policeman is over in Sark for a film

parts.note: Jura is an island of the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it

parts.note: taken as written; Sark is one of the Channel Islands

indicators.note: turned over means read the other way round

explanation.surface: A Scottish island constable has gone over to Sark to see a movie.
explanation.definitionFit: Jurassic Park is Steven Spielberg's 1993 dinosaur film.

clue.text: A US art critic upset Thomas Nast, for example

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An American critic was offended by the work of a famous cartoonist.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Nast was a nineteenth-century American political cartoonist who popularised the modern image of Santa Claus.
explanation.definitionFit: Nast drew exaggerated satirical portraits of politicians, which is the work of a caricaturist.

clue.text: A cab's crashed going over windy canal in Moroccan city

indicators.note: in a down clue, the piece going over another sits above it
a crashed vehicle is a wreck, so its letters end up jumbled
a windy course twists about, so these letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A taxi crashes into a winding canal in a North African city.
explanation.definitionFit: Casablanca is Morocco's largest city and main port.

clue.text: They may be expressly provided for the rest of the Continental passengers

definitions.text: They may be expressly provided for the rest of the Continental passengers

parts.note: surface reading: something specifically supplied for everyone else

parts.words: the rest of the Continental passengers
parts.note: setter's reading: sleeping accommodation on European express trains, where travellers rest

explanation.walkthrough: 'Expressly' hides express trains and 'the rest' means sleep, not 'the remainder'.
explanation.definitionFit: Wagons-lits are French sleeping cars, carriages where long-distance rail passengers can lie down overnight.

clue.text: Leave a ring on

parts.note: a band is a ring, such as a wedding band

explanation.surface: An instruction to keep a ring on your finger.
explanation.definitionFit: To abandon is to desert or walk away from, a synonym of the verb leave.

clue.text: Contact one in salon I refurbished

indicators.note: a refurbished room is rearranged and redone, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Someone is arranging to meet a contact in the hair salon they have just done up.
explanation.definitionFit: A liaison is a link or point of communication between people, much as a contact is.

clue.text: A room's musty stocked with old sherry

indicators.note: a store stocked with goods holds them inside, so one piece goes within the other
something gone musty has decayed and is out of shape, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A stuffy cellar room holds bottles of old sherry.
explanation.definitionFit: Amoroso is a sweetened, dark style of oloroso sherry.

clue.text: Drunken sot, affluent one who ignores home truths?

indicators.note: a drunken person staggers about, so these letters lurch into another order

explanation.surface: A wealthy drunk refuses to face uncomfortable facts about his family life.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the figurative definition: ostriches are said to bury their heads in the sand.
explanation.definitionFit: An ostrich, figuratively, is a person who refuses to face unpleasant realities, from the myth of hiding its head in sand.

clue.text: City left by British in ruins, after bombing

indicators.note: after a bombing everything is blown apart and left in a jumble, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A wartime scene: a city abandoned by the British, lying in ruins after an air raid.
explanation.walkthrough: Lisburn is a city in Northern Ireland, south-west of Belfast.
explanation.definitionFit: Lisburn was granted city status in 2002, so it fits the plain definition City.

clue.text: The father of Odysseus relates badly

indicators.note: something done badly is done wrongly, so the letters come out in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Someone tells the story of Odysseus's father poorly.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Laertes, king of Ithaca, is the father of Odysseus and appears in the Odyssey.

clue.text: Fail to win card game so become exasperated

parts.note: to lose is to fail to win
patience is the British name for solitaire

explanation.surface: Someone keeps losing at cards and finally snaps.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose patience is an idiom for running out of tolerance and getting irritated.

clue.text: Rosemary, for example, is from Frobisher Bay

indicators.note: coming from within the following words means the letters are taken out of them intact

explanation.surface: A woman called Rosemary hails from a bay in the Canadian Arctic.
explanation.walkthrough: Rosemary looks like a woman's name, but it is the cooking plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosemary is an aromatic plant used in cooking, an example of the category.

clue.text: Swimmer in book caught in trap

indicators.note: something caught in a trap is held inside it

parts.note: a spider's web is a trap

explanation.surface: A swimmer from a story ends up tangled in a net.
explanation.walkthrough: Captain Matthew Webb was the first person recorded swimming the English Channel, in 1875.
explanation.definitionFit: Webb is famous as a swimmer, the first to cross the Channel unaided.

clue.text: Catch learner driver, man going the wrong way

indicators.note: travelling the wrong way means read backwards

parts.note: from the L-plate that UK learner drivers display

explanation.surface: Stopping a learner motorist who is driving the wrong way down a road.
explanation.definitionFit: To nail someone is informal for catching or arresting them.

clue.text: Language that may make native seem shocked

indicators.note: something shocked is jolted out of place, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Some coarse language could make a local person look appalled.
explanation.definitionFit: Vietnamese is the national language of Vietnam.

clue.text: Take off around start of summer recess

indicators.note: one piece placed around another encloses it

parts.note: to ape or take off someone is to mimic them

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, the only one kept

explanation.surface: Taking time off at the start of the summer holidays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take off' looks like leaving, but it means imitate.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is a semicircular recess at the end of a church, usually behind the altar.

clue.text: Dish in B&B — his hake's fantastic

indicators.note: something fantastic is fanciful and bizarre, so the letters are freely rearranged

parts.note: the two Bs of bed and breakfast

explanation.surface: A guest-house owner boasts that his fish dish is superb.
explanation.walkthrough: B&B is a bed and breakfast, a small guest house.
explanation.definitionFit: Shish kebab is a dish of meat chunks grilled on a skewer.
